title: fix(repos): registerRepo normalizes path separators to dedupe on Windows
why:
Windows path.join yields a backslash loreDir; the old string-equality dedup
missed existing forward-slash entries, so the same repo registered twice
(real case: mal-analyze-cli + mal-analyze-cli-2 pointing at one .lore).
Normalize to forward slashes before compare and store; both sides normalize
so legacy backslash entries dedupe too. Tests updated for normalized storage.

title: docs(claude): record pid-reuse deadlock & timeout-cliff pitfalls
why:
Two non-obvious failure modes from the jpm-ysqy auto-mode investigation:
runner.pid storing a bare pid let a reused pid (post-reboot) deadlock the
ticker forever; and a 600s per-page timeout sat right at the median
completion time so ~half the component pages never finished. Both are
the kind of thing a refactor would silently reintroduce.

title: fix(runner,syncstate): per-page rewrite timeout 600s→1200s; stale upper bound 90→180min
why:
Auto runs showed component pages timing out at 600s while the one that
succeeded (scripts.md) already took 492s — 82% of the limit. The page
that timed out (art.md) was the *smallest* on disk, so wall-clock is
driven by how much source the LLM reads, not page size; 600s left almost
no margin and ~half the pages never finished, stranding them in the
queue. Raise per-page timeout to 1200s (2.4x the normal completion) and
lift RUNNER_STALE_MS to 180min so a long 5-page round is never misjudged
as a dead pid (which would let the ticker launch a second runner).

title: fix(syncstate,runner,server): runner.pid stale detection — kill pid-reuse deadlock
why:
After a reboot the old runner's pid gets reused by another process;
isAlive(pid) returns true forever so the ticker thinks a runner is
always running and never fires — auto pages never get rewritten (real
case: jpm-ysqy stuck on auto with stale pages). runner.pid now stores a
write timestamp; runnerAlive() requires isAlive AND age < 90min. Legacy
{pid} (no ts) is treated as expired, auto-clearing old residual locks.

title: fix(portal): autostart vbs uses node absolute path — bare 'node' fails in Startup env
why:
Machine reboot didn't bring portal up: the Startup .vbs ran 'node ...'
but the login shell environment has no node on PATH (node lives in
C:\Program Files\nodejs). Now the vbs uses process.execPath (absolute),
so it no longer depends on PATH. CLAUDE.md resident stats refreshed by
finalize.
